title: How to Use ChatGPT Dots to Build Apps in Minutes (AI + No Code)
promo_conflict: The video is a tutorial for the AI tools Dots and Base 44. Sponsor reads were cut out, so it may be sponsored or affiliate content. The app idea came from Dots and was never launched or sold, so there is no evidence it makes money.

stated_problem.quote: and they want a faster more consistent way to turn their content into something more polished.
stated_problem.speaker: Mikey (Mikey No Code)

idea.name: Carousel Studio (branded LinkedIn carousel maker)
idea.one_liner: A browser-based web app that independent consultants use to turn their content into branded LinkedIn document carousels, exported as PDF or PNG. It would presumably make money from a subscription, though no pricing is given.
idea.customer: Independent consultants who regularly post LinkedIn document carousels
idea.offer: A carousel editor with a fixed slide structure (cover, content and closing slides), a reusable brand kit, design presets, a 'paste to slides' import from plain text, a local project library, export checks, LinkedIn PDF and PNG zip export, and JSON backup and restore

key_quotes.quote: And out of those options, the branded carousel maker does stand out to me the most here.
The target user is very clear and there is already a reason someone might actually pay for it.
It works especially well for this kind of project because the sort of scope it's small enough for a proof of concept.
Dots also makes it clear here that all of this should happen locally inside of the browser without cloud rendering uploads or any new back-end features.

ideas.delivery: A self-serve web app built with no code by prompting Base 44 in three phases planned by Dots. Everything runs in the browser with local storage and no backend. Only a proof of concept was built and tested by the host. It has no users, pricing or launch.
ideas.other_uk_rules: If it becomes a paid subscription, the DMCC Act subscription rules apply (clear pre-contract information, reminders and easy cancellation). Storing data only in the browser keeps UK GDPR exposure low, but adding accounts or cloud storage would make the founder a data controller. Consumer Contracts Regulations would also apply to cancellation rights for any non-business buyers.
